archetype: Naya Dinosaur battlecruiser, and strategic_frame.json's label — 'a linear critical-mass ramp deck whose payoff density is compressed into one commander combat trigger' — is right about the intent. The measurement disagrees about which engine carries the deck. The enrage web is drawn 82.4% of games and 72.6% by turn six; the commander is cast by turn six in 8.3%. On the numbers this is an enrage-value midrange deck that also happens to run an eight-mana commander, and it should be built that way.
verdict: This deck interacts better than most typal lists and it converts: 11 removal copies inside an 18-card interactive suite, all five permanent classes covered, 34 creatures, and four checker-passed lines including a genuinely one-sided sweep. What limits it is card advantage, at a narrower scope than the raw count suggests. The axis reads 6 against a target of 10; reading the cards, eight of the 99 do refuel from an empty board, but exactly one of them repeats — Bonehoard Dracosaur, at five mana — and three of the four that cost three hand you a land rather than a spell. That matters because every one of the deck's six declared components is assembled by drawing cards, and four of them sit between 48.5% and 62.3% by turn six. Card flow is the one input upstream of all six at once.

axes.reading: This is the axis that binds, at a scope narrower than the count. Read every card: eight refuel from an empty board — Huatli, Cultivate and Kodama's Reach at three for a land in hand, Monster Manual's Zoological Study at three for a creature, Pantlaza at five, Bonehoard Dracosaur at five, Trumpeting Carnosaur at six, Vaultborn Tyrant at seven, which does trigger on its own entry. But only Bonehoard Dracosaur REPEATS without a board; every other boardless refuel fires once, and everything that repeats — Garruk's Uprising, Curious Altisaur, Ripjaw Raptor, Selvala, Descendants' Path, and Pantlaza's and Vaultborn Tyrant's later triggers — wants a board, a connection or damage first. So the deck can find a land while stalled; it cannot find a second one cheaply, and it has one repeating engine to draw toward at five mana. (Jetmir's Garden, which the audit probes, cycles for {3}: card-neutral, not card advantage.)

open_questions.question: Does a Forerunner of the Empire ping with Wrathful Raptors on the battlefield still mark damage on your own Dinosaurs — feeding Ranging Raptors, Ripjaw Raptor and Polyraptor enrage — or is that damage converted into redirects, so the reach comes at the cost of the engine?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All five cards are in the 99 and no checker-passed stack has ever had them share a board: stack 005 resolved the ping web without Wrathful Raptors, stack 004 resolved Wrathful Raptors without the web. The answer decides whether Wrathful Raptors is an engine piece or an engine-killer in the deck's most available component.

open_questions.question: What do Knight of the Stampede, Kinjalli's Caller, Herald's Horn and Drover of the Mighty do to the commander cast curve, and what do the eight unmodelled land-fetch effects do to the available-mana curve?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The simulator states it models neither cost reducers, nor extra card draw, nor the land-fetch ramp — only '{T}: Add' producers. So every mana-side figure about casting Gishath (8.3% by turn six, mean 7.969, available mana peaking at 7.321 on turn ten) is a floor, and this diagnosis deliberately grounds its binding claim on the draw-side assembly rates instead, which that gap does not touch. Extending the model would say how much of the eight-mana problem is real.

open_questions.question: Do Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth pull the pivot turn forward, and by how much?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame.json leans on both as the answer to the 7.969 mean and the simulator models neither. If they are worth two turns, the eight-mana problem is smaller than the axis reading implies; if they are not, the cost-reducer component is the only lever left.

open_questions.question: Is there doctrine on board-contingent card advantage — engines that draw only once the board exists — and on cheat-into-play as an archetype axis?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The binding finding here is not that the deck has 6 draw pieces but that nine of ten require a board. strategy:deckbuilding.ratios budgets card draw by count, and nothing in the corpus distinguishes refuel-while-behind from convert-while-ahead. strategic_frame.json's gaps list already names the cheat-into-play hole.

gaps: The goldfish models neither cost reducers, nor extra card draw, nor the eight effects here that put lands onto the battlefield (Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Topiary Stomper, Ranging Raptors, Krosan Verge, Myriad Landscape), because it counts only '{T}: Add' producers — verbatim in meta.model_assumptions. Every mana-side commander-cast figure quoted here is therefore a ceiling on the problem, not the expectation, and no claim in this diagnosis rests on one alone. Settled by a goldfish model extension.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit's freshness block reports recon absent), so nothing in this diagnosis leans on inclusion rates or on what other Gishath lists run. Every add is argued from this deck's own measured axes.

The obsolescence index proposes Three Visits over Skyshroud Claim and Farseek over Kodama's Reach on 'Lower CMC' alone. Read the cards: Skyshroud Claim fetches two Forests untapped and Kodama's Reach nets a land into hand, so the index's advantage is a mana-value comparison, not a fit judgment. No swap is proposed on that basis.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so deck-audit's freshness block cannot confirm it is current; the floor-4 figure here was re-derived by running bracket-check against the present 99 rather than read from the file.

card_roles.json classifies 94.4% of this deck; Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede, Rishkar's Expertise and Triumphant Chomp carry no role at all, so every axis count above is a floor. Two of those five (Hunter's Insight, Rishkar's Expertise) are card draw the card-advantage axis cannot see.

No checker-passed stack's scenario names any of the four proposed cuts, so none of them orphans a verified line. Blasphemous Act (004), Temple Altisaur (004, 005) and Polyraptor (002, 003, 005) do carry verified lines and were deliberately left alone.

SCOPE CORRECTION, iteration 2. An earlier draft of this diagnosis claimed only Bonehoard Dracosaur refuels from an empty board. That is false: Vaultborn Tyrant triggers on its own entry, and Huatli, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Zoological Study, Pantlaza and Trumpeting Carnosaur all work with no board. The surviving claim is narrower — one REPEATING boardless refuel, at five mana — and the prescription was resized to match: Guardian Project was dropped from the add list because it answers the count rather than the shape, leaving one card-advantage add (Herald's Horn) instead of two.

Whether the narrowed card-advantage gap or the 16-source colour shortfall is the larger real cost is not settled by any artifact here. Colour-sources is measured hypergeometrically and is immune to the goldfish's modelling gap; card-advantage is argued from the six components' draw-side assembly rates. Both readings are recorded; only one add is spent on each.
